Overview

1. Introduction & Getting Started

Everything you need to make your first API call.

Base URL

All endpoints are relative to a single base URL configured as an environment variable:

{{API_URL}} — set this environment variable before making any request. The value is deployment-specific and provided by your Songa administrator.

Request Format

All request bodies must be sent as JSON with the header Content-Type: application/json. Date-time values must conform to ISO 8601 (e.g. 2025-12-16T06:21:56.397Z). Array filter parameters may be passed either as a JSON body on GET requests or as repeated query string keys where noted.

Response Format

All responses are JSON-encoded. Successful requests return HTTP 2xx. A typical success response wraps data in a top-level object. Error responses include an HTTP 4xx or 5xx status code and a JSON body containing at minimum a message field describing the failure.

Versioning & Stability

This document corresponds to the API state for Phase 9. Breaking changes will be communicated via a new versioned document. Endpoints prefixed /ussd/ relate to the USSD gateway integration and require additional third-party configuration (see Tenants → Config).

Overview

2. Authentication Guide

How JWT Bearer tokens work in the Songa API.

⚠️ Note: Every protected endpoint requires a valid Bearer token in the Authorization HTTP header. Tokens are short-lived and must be refreshed by re-authenticating via the login endpoint.

Step 1 — Obtain a Token

Send a POST request to /auth/login with your credentials. A successful response returns a signed JWT. Store this token securely — treat it as a password.

Web login: "email" + "password"
Mobile login: additionally pass "userId" and "isMobile": true.

Step 2 — Attach the Token

Include the token in every subsequent request header:

Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

Step 3 — Handle Expiry

Tokens expire after 24 hours. When a request returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized, re-authenticate by calling POST /auth/login again.

For password resets: (1) POST /auth/forgot-password → triggers an email with a reset token, (2) POST /auth/reset-password with that token and a new password.

User Roles

The role field in user objects maps to the following access levels:

ValueDescription
1Super Admin — full platform access across all tenants
2Driver — mobile app access: trips, kilikawi and rentals only
3Fleet Manager — manage permissions from admin panel
Overview

3. Error Codes & HTTP Status Reference

Standard HTTP semantics as used in the Songa API.

StatusNameMeaning in Songa APIRecommended Action
200OKRequest succeeded; data returned in response body.Process response normally.
201CreatedResource successfully created (e.g. new trike, driver).Use returned ID for follow-up requests.
204No ContentSuccess with no body (e.g. delete operations).Treat as success.
400Bad RequestMalformed JSON, missing required field, or invalid value.Check request body against schema.
401UnauthorizedMissing, expired, or invalid Bearer token.Re-authenticate via POST /auth/login.
403ForbiddenAuthenticated but insufficient role/permission.Verify user role; escalate if needed.
404Not FoundResource with the given ID does not exist.Verify the ID and retry.
409ConflictDuplicate registration number or unique constraint violation.Use a different identifier.
422Unprocessable EntitySemantically invalid input (e.g. invalid enum value).Validate enum values before sending.
429Too Many RequestsRate limit exceeded.Implement exponential back-off.
500Internal Server ErrorUnexpected server-side failure.Retry once; contact support if persistent.
503Service UnavailableServer temporarily overloaded or under maintenance.Retry after a short delay.
